facts.value: not later than the next regular payday
facts.summary: Iowa: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the next regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: When the employment of an employee is suspended or terminated, the employer shall pay all wages earned ... not later than the next regular payday for the pay period in which the wages were earned
facts.source_title: Iowa Code 91A.4 (2026), Employment suspension or termination
facts.notes: Commission true-ups due within 30 days (same section).

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Iowa basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 The Iowa minimum wage equals the federal minimum wage rate if it is set below the federal rate.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Iowa: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Weekly; Bi-weekly (note 6); Semi-monthly; Monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 6: Iowa.  Employers are required to pay most employees via a regular payday at least biweekly, semimonthly or monthly. Any predictable and reliable pay schedule is permitted as long as employees get paid at least monthly and no later than 12 days (excluding Sundays and legal holidays) from the end of the period when the wages were earned. This can be waived by written agreement; employees on commission have different requirements. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.summary: Iowa is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
